basis: Intellectual developmental disorder with defining skeletal anomalies; micrognathia 4/4 and short fifth fingers 2/4. Hearing impairment and scoliosis each 1/4.
Primary carcinoma arising in the lung; no additional organ involvement established at >=30%.
Inherited progressive skin pigmentation disorder; no established damage to other organ axes.
Cortical malformations, intellectual disability, seizures and peripheral neuropathy are neurologic. Foot and hand proportions do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Umbrella of TRPV4-related skeletal dysplasias; neurologic TRPV4 disorders are distinct phenotypes.
Bilateral congenital shortening and fusion of digits of the hands and feet.
Primary immunodeficiency defined by defective neutrophil function and leukocytosis. Abscesses and bacterial infections are secondary infections, not additional intrinsic organ disease.
Macrophage-mediated inflammatory lesions of skeletal muscle and fascia; weakness is common. Fever, fatigue and arthralgia do not establish other organ damage.
Inherited susceptibility to febrile seizures; seizures define a neurologic disorder without additional established organ damage.
Congenital limb malformation with complete syndactyly and frequent polydactyly; cutaneous digit fusion does not indicate a separate skin disorder.
Predominantly reproductive gonadal germ-cell malignancy. Pineal primaries are uncommon; the definition establishes no metastatic organ affected in >=30% across the group.
Pectoral muscle aplasia defines the syndrome. Subcutaneous fat absence is reported in 80-99% and renal hypoplasia in 30-79%; breast anomalies have no axis.
Systemic measles virus infection. Rash and respiratory symptoms are transient; damaging pneumonia, encephalitis and other organ complications affect a minority.
Zellweger spectrum metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction, hepatic disease and retinal degeneration are common (>=30%). Common hearing loss omitted at the four-axis cap.
Severe CNS impairment is defining; heart defects ~80%, eye malformations ~50-70% and cleft lip/palate ~60% cause direct abnormalities. Polydactyly omitted at cap.
Complete failure of atrioventricular electrical conduction is intrinsic cardiac dysfunction.
Lipomas 7/7 and follicular skin tumors 5/7 define the phenotype. Renal carcinoma 3/7 is a separate predisposed malignancy; pulmonary involvement is unestablished for BHD2.
Platelet granule deficiency causes thrombocytopenia, impaired aggregation and bleeding; no separate organ damage is established as common.
Congenital urethral obstruction directly damages the urinary tract and renal function. Recurrent urinary infections are separate secondary infections.
Microcephaly/intellectual disability and severe nephropathy define GAMOS7; kidney failure 11/12. Eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 2/3; cardiac and skeletal disease are uncommon.
Inherited skeletal muscle hyperirritability with rippling, mounding, hypertrophy and cramps; EMG abnormalities do not imply a separate nerve disorder.
Insulin-secreting tumor of endocrine pancreatic beta cells. Hypoglycemic neurologic symptoms do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Available syndrome description establishes ectrodactyly, syndactyly and duplicated great toes. Hydrops alone does not establish cardiac or other specific organ damage.
ID and renal anomalies define syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss and persistent neutropenia each 30-79%. Camptodactyly also 30-79%, omitted at cap; cardiac data limited.
Non-syndromic congenital duplication of a developed postaxial digit; no other organ involvement applies across the group.
